title: Exalted far above every flaw, and still knows your whisper
subtitle: Al-Muta'ali: the Supremely Exalted, above every likeness and every limit
intro: Al-Muta'ali (الْمُتَعَالِي) means The Supremely Exalted: Allah rises infinitely above every flaw, every limitation and every likeness to His creation, and above everything by His power. It is the meaning inside the ta'ala Muslims say after His name. Yet the one verse that names Him so also says your secret and your spoken word are the same to Him.

root.sense: From 'uluw, height. The form muta'ali (from ta'ala) conveys rising above, transcending, being exalted beyond reach. The everyday phrase Allah ta'ala, Allah the Exalted, comes from it. Where 'ali names height as an attribute, muta'ali emphasizes how far He transcends anything that could be compared to Him or said against Him.

row.title: Every false claim
sub: a son, a partner, a rival

knowing: Al-Muta'ali appears once in the Quran, in a verse of breathtaking compression: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Great, the Supremely Exalted (13:9). {idea}It means He is exalted above every imperfection, above every resemblance to what He created, and above everything by His power over it{/idea}. No weakness, no need, no limit, no rival, no comparison reaches Him.

It differs from Al-Aliyy. Al-Aliyy affirms that He is high in essence, rank and power. Al-Muta'ali adds the sense of transcendence: whatever people imagine, invent or say about God, He is beyond it. That is why the Quran so often says: exalted is He, ta'ala, high above what they associate with Him, and high above what they say, a great exaltation (17:43).

Every time you say Allah ta'ala or subhanahu wa ta'ala, you are using this name's meaning. {reward}It keeps your idea of God clean: not a bigger human, not a force of nature, but the One beyond all likeness.{/reward}
seeing: Read the verses around it. Just before: Allah knows what every womb carries, what it lacks and what it adds, and everything with Him is by measure (13:8). Just after: it is the same to Him whether you hide your speech or say it aloud, whether you hide by night or walk openly by day (13:10). The Supremely Exalted is placed between the womb and the whisper.

That is the Quran's way of correcting two errors at once. {trap}Some imagine God so high that He is absent from daily life; others imagine Him so near that He becomes like a creature.{/trap} Al-Muta'ali is exalted beyond every likeness, and His knowledge misses nothing: not a heartbeat in the dark of the womb, not a word whispered at night.
trusting: When you feel your situation is too small for the Lord of the worlds, a minor worry about a child, a private shame, a fear you have never told anyone, {idea}remember that the One named Al-Muta'ali in 13:9 is described in 13:10 as hearing your hidden speech exactly as clearly as your loud speech{/idea}. Being exalted does not make Him distant.

And when you feel overwhelmed by people's claims, ideologies that mock faith, voices that reduce God to a myth, Al-Muta'ali is your calm. {reward}Nothing said against Him touches Him. He remains Supremely Exalted, and so does the truth you hold.{/reward}
loving: We are drawn to greatness that is pure: no hidden flaws, no ego, no limits. Al-Muta'ali is greatness without a single shadow. {reward}And the heart melts when it realizes that this transcendent Lord has chosen to know every detail of its life, from the womb onward, with perfect care.{/reward}
now: Late at night you type a worry into a search engine that you would never say aloud. Before you hit enter, stop. {idea}The Supremely Exalted already heard it, as clearly as if you had shouted it (13:10).{/idea} Close the tab, and say it to Him instead.
old: God is so exalted that my private worries are beneath His notice.
new: Al-Muta'ali is beyond every limit, which is exactly why nothing about me escapes Him.
try: Each time you say Allah ta'ala or subhanahu wa ta'ala today, pause for a second to mean it: He is exalted above everything I could imagine.

dua.text: Ya Muta'ali, You are exalted above every flaw and every likeness, and my secret and my speech are the same to You. Purify my belief in You, hear what I cannot say aloud, and raise me by Your mercy.
dua.note: Call on Al-Muta'ali when your belief needs purifying or your worries feel too private to voice, recalling 13:9-10.

pairs.why: Joined in their only shared verse, 13:9: the Great and the Supremely Exalted, greatness and transcendence together.
13:9 opens with His knowledge of the unseen and seen: the Exalted One is never distant from what He created.
Al-Quddus is His purity from every defect; Al-Muta'ali is His exaltation far above them and above all likeness.

faq.a: Al-Muta'ali means The Supremely Exalted. It describes Allah as transcending every imperfection, every limitation and every likeness to His creation, and as being above all things by His power. It is the meaning behind the phrase Allah ta'ala.

faq.q: Where is Al-Muta'ali mentioned in the Quran?
faq.a: Once, in 13:9: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Great, the Supremely Exalted. The very next verse says it is the same to Him whether one hides speech or says it openly, showing that His exaltation does not make Him distant.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Aliyy and Al-Muta'ali?
faq.a: Al-Aliyy affirms that Allah is the Most High in essence, rank and power. Al-Muta'ali, from a form that conveys transcendence, stresses that He is exalted far above anything people imagine or attribute to Him and above every resemblance to creation.

faq.q: What does subhanahu wa ta'ala mean?
faq.a: It means glorified is He and exalted. Subhanahu declares Allah free of every imperfection; ta'ala declares Him exalted above everything, the meaning of the name Al-Muta'ali. Muslims say it after mentioning Allah out of reverence.
